basis: love rejoices with the truth
note: Paul says love does not rejoice in wrongdoing but rejoices with truth; this gives the commentary's haqq a communal ethical setting, where truth marks the difference between right and wrong action.

basis: love bears and endures all things
note: Paul describes love as bearing and enduring all things; this supplies a relational form of sabr alongside the commentary's reciprocal counsel, distinct from mere aim or force.

basis: labor not in vain
note: The commentary juxtaposes universal loss with directed good work; Paul urges steadfast abundance in the Lord's work because such labor is not in vain, specifying the exception to futility.

basis: running without aim and boxing the air rejected
note: Paul says he does not run aimlessly or box as one beating air; this names the wasted, off-target action that the commentary uses khusr to evoke, and makes disciplined direction the condition for effective effort.

basis: blow that does not miss
note: The commentary's worked spear and unswerving thrust make accuracy central; Paul says he boxes without beating the air, turning directed effort into a test of disciplined action.

basis: no lie from truth
note: The commentary sets haqq against the false that it destroys; the letter tells its addressees that no lie comes from truth, making their opposition categorical.

basis: truth versus error
note: The commentary's claim that after truth comes deviation has a precise alternative here: receptivity to apostolic testimony distinguishes the spirit of truth from the spirit of error.

basis: straying sheep return
note: The commentary makes loss a move off the line; Peter tells his addressees they had been straying like sheep but have now returned to the shepherd of their souls.

basis: suffering while doing good
note: The verse's exception combines righteous deeds and patience; Peter asks those who suffer in accordance with God's will to entrust themselves to the faithful Creator while continuing to do good.

basis: admonish, encourage, help, and be patient with all
note: Paul assigns mutual correction and encouragement for different members of the community, then patience toward all; this closely joins the commentary's reciprocal counsel with its sabr, while spelling out whom that care serves.

basis: admonish with patience
note: The verse joins reciprocal counsel and sabr; Paul asks the community to admonish the idle, encourage the fainthearted, help the weak and be patient with everyone.

basis: pursue faith righteousness endurance
note: The commentary treats right action as force aimed on a line; Timothy is told to pursue righteousness, faith and endurance, putting the verse's qualities into directed motion.

basis: weapons demolish strongholds
note: Paul's weapons are powerful for demolishing strongholds; this gives the commentary's haqq-against-batil image an inward, nonmaterial battle setting rather than a physical spear.

basis: weapons demolish strongholds
note: The commentary presents truth as an impact that breaks falsehood; Paul's weapons have divine power to demolish strongholds in an argument over knowledge and obedience.

basis: arguments pulled down and thoughts taken captive
note: Paul names arguments raised against knowledge of God and says thoughts are taken captive; this specifies the inner target of the weapons in the preceding verse, analogous to the commentary's blow that reaches inward.

basis: arguments brought down
note: The commentary says haqq reaches and overcomes its opposing target; Paul describes demolishing arguments raised against knowledge of God and bringing thoughts captive, specifying the intellectual target of the preceding weapons.

basis: word of truth and righteous weapons
note: The commentary lets truth function as a directed weapon; Paul places the word of truth and God's power beside weapons of righteousness in his account of ministry.

basis: forsaken straight way
note: The commentary interprets loss as leaving the line; the false teachers have abandoned the straight way and gone astray, tying moral error to misdirected travel.

basis: faith and endurance under attack
note: The verse's believers recommend patience; Paul boasts of the community's steadfastness and faith amid persecutions and afflictions, giving sabr a social setting of pressure.

basis: worker handles word of truth rightly
note: The commentary joins amal as directed effort to haqq as an unswerving result; Timothy is told to be an approved worker who handles the word of truth rightly and need not be ashamed.

basis: preach the word, correct and exhort with patience
note: Paul tells Timothy to proclaim the word, correct, rebuke, and exhort with all patience; this closely combines the commentary's truth and reciprocal advice with sabr as the manner of correction.

basis: exhort with patience and teaching
note: The verse couples recommending truth with patience; Timothy is instructed to proclaim the word, correct and exhort with complete patience and teaching.

basis: listeners are pierced in the heart by Peter's proclamation
note: After Peter's speech, listeners are pierced in the heart and ask what to do; this gives the commentary's truthful impact an inward human response and connects penetration to changed action.

basis: speech cuts to the heart
note: The commentary's truth blow reaches within; after Peter's address the hearers are pierced in the heart and ask what to do, making inward impact lead to action.

basis: faith does not shift
note: The commentary's faithful workers must keep from swerving into loss; Colossians conditions its hope on continuing in faith, established and steadfast, without moving away from the gospel's hope.

basis: Christ's word teaches and admonishes people mutually
note: The community is to let Christ's word dwell richly as its members teach and admonish one another; this gives the commentary's mutual counsel to truth a word-centered communal form, with song and thanksgiving as its setting.

basis: teach and admonish one another
note: The verse says believers mutually commend truth; Colossians asks that Christ's word dwell in them as they teach and admonish one another in wisdom, supplying an explicit communal verbal act.

basis: patience, bearing with one another in love
note: Ephesians describes communal life through patience and bearing with one another; this gives the commentary's sabr a specifically relational practice, though it does not repeat its advice-to-one-another formula.

basis: truth spoken to each neighbor as members of one body
note: After rejecting falsehood, Ephesians commands each person to speak truth to a neighbor because they are members of one another; this is a concrete communal form of the commentary's mutual exhortation to haqq.

basis: speak truth to one another
note: The verse's tawasaw bil haqq is mutual; Ephesians tells each person to put off falsehood and speak truth with a neighbor because they belong to one another.

basis: truth as belt and righteousness as breastplate
note: In Paul's battle equipment, truth and righteousness protect the body rather than serve as the commentary's offensive thrust; the shared pairing clarifies how the same virtues can be imagined as guarding against error.

basis: truth equips the fighter
note: The commentary's directed work and haqq meet in combat imagery; the exhortation has believers fasten truth around the waist as part of their equipment before naming the word as a sword.

basis: sword of the Spirit identified as God's word
note: In the armor passage, the Spirit's sword is God's word; this makes the commentary's forceful action a verbal weapon, while Ephesians places it among the community's defensive equipment.

basis: word as sword
note: The commentary's directed work and penetrating truth meet the instruction to take the sword of the Spirit, identified as God's word, as a weapon in a struggle.

basis: persevere in doing good
note: The verse pairs right action and sabr; Paul urges hearers not to grow weary in doing good because a harvest comes if they do not give up.

basis: stir one another to love and good works
note: Hebrews tells its hearers to consider how to stir one another toward love and good works; this gives a specific communal practice corresponding to the commentary's repeated mutual exhortation and directed action.

basis: spur one another to good works
note: The verse combines good deeds with mutual urging; Hebrews asks its audience to consider how to stimulate one another to love and good works.

basis: meeting together and encouraging one another
note: Hebrews joins continued assembly to mutual encouragement as the day approaches; it adds the gathered setting for the commentary's reciprocal counsel and the persistence implied by sabr.

basis: endurance after doing God's will
note: The verse pairs action and patient persistence; Hebrews says the audience needs endurance so that, after doing God's will, they may receive the promise.

basis: run the set race with endurance
note: Hebrews tells its hearers to run the race set before them with endurance; this combines the commentary's straight-course image with sabr, making patient persistence the means of staying on course.

basis: run with endurance
note: The commentary ties directed action to sabr; Hebrews calls for endurance in the race set before the community, a sustained course rather than a single unswerving thrust.

basis: make straight paths for the feet so the lame may heal
note: Hebrews commands straight paths for feet so the lame limb may be healed rather than dislocated; this combines the commentary's straight trajectory with its bodily penetration image, and turns straightness toward restoration.

basis: daily mutual exhortation guards against sin's deception
note: Hebrews commands daily mutual exhortation so no one hardens through sin's deceit; this links the commentary's counsel in truth to preventing a person's deviation and adds a daily communal practice.

basis: exhort one another against deceit
note: The verse's mutual counsel in truth prevents loss by deviation; Hebrews commands daily reciprocal exhortation so that sin's deceit does not harden anyone.

basis: God's word sharper than a two-edged sword, reaching joints and marrow
note: Hebrews describes God's living word as penetrating to the body's innermost divisions and judging thoughts; it closely matches the commentary's strike that passes through to the inside, while locating the penetration in discernment.

basis: word as piercing sword
note: The commentary imagines haqq as a blow that reaches inside; God's word here is sharper than a two edged sword and penetrates to the division of soul and spirit, making inward reach the point of the image.

basis: inward exposure after piercing word
note: The commentary's blow reaches the inside; the continuation of the piercing word says no creature is hidden and all are exposed before God, identifying what the inward reach discloses.

basis: testing produces endurance
note: James says the testing of faith produces endurance; this describes sabr as formed under pressure, giving the commentary's human target image a process of remaining steadfast through impact.

basis: endurance completes its work so one lacks nothing
note: James says endurance should complete its work so a person becomes complete and lacks nothing; this joins the commentary's sabr and amal to an explicit overcoming of lack.

basis: endurance removes lack
note: The verse's sabr belongs to the exception from loss; James says steadfastness must complete its work so the believers are complete and lacking nothing, joining endurance to the opposite of deficiency.

basis: faith requires works
note: The commentary turns amal into exertion with effect; James says faith by itself is dead if it has no works, giving the verse's faith and righteous action an explicit relation.

basis: faith works together with deeds
note: The exception joins believing and doing; James says Abraham's faith was active together with his works and completed by them, making the pairing operative rather than merely adjacent.

basis: tongue as destroying fire
note: The commentary's effective truth is cast against its opponent; James calls the tongue a fire that stains the body and sets a life's course ablaze, a contrary example of speech as uncontrolled destructive force.

basis: one among the community wanders from the truth and is brought back
note: James describes a believer wandering from truth and another person bringing him back; this closely joins the commentary's deviation from the line to its mutual counsel in haqq.

basis: turning a sinner back saves a soul from death
note: James says the person who turns a sinner back from his erring way saves him from death; this makes correction of deviation a concrete rescue from loss.

basis: way and truth joined
note: The commentary joins haqq with the path that avoids deviation; Jesus calls himself the way and the truth and the life, locating true direction in a person in this passage.

basis: God's word identified as truth
note: The commentary's haqq functions through a forceful utterance; Jesus asks that his disciples be sanctified in truth and identifies God's word as truth, giving the verbal and moral terms a direct link.

basis: a soldier pierces Jesus' side with a spear
note: John recounts a soldier piercing Jesus' side and blood and water emerging; this is a literal bodily counterpart to the commentary's lance entering the inside, while its passion context makes the pierced person a victim rather than a target of righteous counsel.

basis: lying speech and murder joined
note: The commentary opposes truth to falsehood as a forceful conflict; Jesus calls the devil a murderer and the father of lies, giving false speech a destructive agent rather than a neutral wrong turn.

basis: lost sheep sought
note: The commentary equates loss with going astray; the shepherd in Jesus' question goes after the one lost sheep until he finds it, giving the lost state an active remedy.

basis: sword pierces soul
note: The commentary's thrust penetrates inward; Simeon tells Mary a sword will pierce her own soul and thoughts of many hearts will be revealed, making interior wounding disclose what is hidden.

basis: Isaiah's wilderness oracle assigned to John's preaching
note: Luke introduces the Isaiah quotation as the word of God coming to John in the wilderness; this Christian reception relocates the road-preparation image into John's public call, complementing the straightened-path detail in the following verse.

basis: Isaiah's crooked road applied to John's call to prepare
note: Luke applies Isaiah's road-making language to John's wilderness preaching: crooked ways are made straight as people prepare for the Lord. This Christian reading turns the commentary's khusr-as-deviation into a call for moral preparation.

basis: word held fast, fruit borne with patience
note: In Jesus' explanation of the good soil, hearers hold fast the word and bear fruit with patience; this joins inward reception, good action, and sabr in one image, adding a fruitful alternative to the commentary's missed or misdirected strike.

basis: one sheep goes astray
note: The commentary's khusr is deviation; Jesus describes a sheep that has strayed and the owner leaving the ninety nine to seek it, making recovery the response to lost direction.

basis: the broad road leads to destruction
note: Jesus describes a broad way leading to destruction; this makes the commentary's khusr-as-deviation a path with a stated end, and contrasts the many who take it with the ayah's exception.

basis: the narrow way leads to life and few find it
note: Jesus contrasts the difficult way leading to life, found by few, with destruction's broad way; this adds the exception's narrow, directed course to the commentary's loss-as-deviation image.

basis: word held through labor without vain result
note: The commentary contrasts lost effort with a true directed word; Paul asks the community to hold fast the word of life so he can say he neither ran nor labored in vain.

basis: press toward goal
note: The commentary's amal is exertion aimed at a target; Paul presses on toward the goal for the prize of God's call, making directed effort explicit without a striking weapon.

basis: sword from mouth
note: The commentary reads haqq as a penetrating projectile; John's vision gives the exalted figure a sharp two edged sword issuing from his mouth, a recurring image of forceful utterance.

basis: endurance and faith of saints
note: The exception joins faith with sabr; this call amid captivity and death names the endurance and faith of the saints, an earlier formulation of the combination.

basis: saints' endurance with God's commandments and faith
note: Revelation identifies the saints by endurance, keeping God's commandments, and faith; this directly brings sabr together with belief and action, adding an apocalyptic picture of the ayah's exception.

basis: faith obedience endurance
note: The exception to human loss names faith, right action and sabr; Revelation identifies the saints by endurance, keeping God's commandments and faith in Jesus under pressure.

basis: rider called Faithful and True wages righteous war
note: Before the mouth-sword appears, the rider is called Faithful and True and judges and makes war in righteousness; this binds truth and right judgment to the force of the strike, as the commentary binds haqq to its direct hit.

basis: sword from the rider's mouth strikes nations
note: The apocalyptic rider's mouth-sword strikes the nations; this makes utterance itself a weapon, close to the commentary's haqq hurled against batil, and adds a public judgment scene.

basis: mouth sword strikes nations
note: The commentary's truth is hurled to strike falsehood; a sharp sword comes from the rider's mouth to strike the nations, similarly giving utterance a weapon's impact.

basis: mouth sword fights error
note: The commentary's truth strikes what has deviated; the speaker commands repentance and threatens to fight the offenders with the sword of his mouth, giving verbal judgment a stated target.

basis: works faith endurance
note: The exception combines belief, deeds and patience; the address to Thyatira names works, faith and endurance together and commends later works greater than earlier ones.

basis: works toil endurance
note: The exception combines deeds and patience; the address to Ephesus names its works, toil and endurance and says it cannot bear evil people.

basis: enduring without weariness
note: The commentary's right effort must keep its course; the same address says the community has endured for the speaker's name and has not grown weary.

basis: word of patient endurance
note: The commentary pairs truth counsel with patience; the address says its hearers have kept the speaker's word of endurance, joining faithful response to utterance with perseverance.

basis: steadfast endurance in doing good
note: Paul describes people who persist in doing good while seeking glory and honor; this directly joins the commentary's amal and sabr, adding an eschatological outcome to sustained action.

basis: patient good work seeks life
note: The exception names righteous action and sabr in response to loss; Paul describes people seeking eternal life through patient persistence in good work.

basis: believers devoted to good works
note: The exception names those who believe and do good deeds; Titus urges those who have believed God to devote themselves to good works, matching that sequence as practical instruction.

basis: word descends as warrior
note: The commentary cites truth being thrown upon falsehood; Wisdom depicts God's all powerful word leaping from the royal throne like a stern warrior into the doomed land, joining divine utterance to forceful arrival.

basis: word carries sharp sword
note: The commentary's truth penetrates and destroys its opponent; Wisdom's personified divine word bears the sharp sword of God's command and fills the land with death, making the weapon an enacted judgment.

basis: well aimed lightning arrows
note: The commentary stresses a blow without deviation; Wisdom describes lightning bolts launched like arrows from a drawn bow against the ungodly, adding explicit aim to the divine attack image.

basis: messianic figure's fiery breath destroys the gathered enemy
note: In Ezra's vision, the human-like deliverer routs the assembled enemy with fire issuing from his mouth rather than a hand-held weapon; this is a distinct apocalyptic version of the commentary's forceful word, replacing the spear's penetration with consuming breath.

basis: truth cast down in dispute over humanity
note: The commentary cites God hurling truth against falsehood while the human stands in loss; the midrash has Truth object to humanity's creation because humans lie, then God casts Truth to the ground, changing the direction and target of the cast.

basis: straight path chosen by a person
note: The commentary makes human action an aimed course that can deviate; the mishnah asks which straight path a person should choose and evaluates the path by honor to the doer and from others.

basis: Moses' raised hands re-read as Israel's upward attention
note: The Mishnah asks whether Moses' hands themselves won the battle, then says Israel prevailed when they looked upward and submitted their hearts to God; this interpretation shifts Exodus' battle image from bodily force to directed communal attention, a useful counter-reading beside the commentary's aimed strike.

basis: word lodged like arrow in flesh
note: The commentary brings together a penetrating weapon, an inward bodily destination and speech; Sirach likens a word lodged inside a fool to an arrow stuck in a person's thigh, though its point is the fool's urge to let the word out.

basis: iniquity as a two-edged sword with incurable wounds
note: Sirach says wrongdoing itself is a two-edged sword whose wounds cannot be healed; beside the commentary's forceful true blow against falsehood, it assigns the piercing weapon to sin and its damage to the victim.

basis: tongue's blow breaks bones
note: Sirach contrasts a whip's bruise with a tongue's blow that breaks bones; it gives speech the commentary's bodily force and inward reach, while emphasizing harmful speech rather than haqq.

basis: tongue blow breaks bones
note: The commentary hears an inward striking force in haqq; Sirach says a tongue's blow can break bones, treating speech as bodily violence in a warning about harmful talk.

basis: more are fallen by the tongue than by the sword
note: Sirach says more people fall through the tongue than through the sword; this intensifies the commentary's weapon image by making speech more destructive than physical arms.

basis: tongue kills more than sword
note: The commentary's verbal truth has a weapon's effect; Sirach compares deaths by sword with still more falls caused by the tongue, emphasizing the dangerous reach of words.

basis: source word ٱلْإِنسَٰن root ء ن س / Aramaic אֱנָשׁ; table's sound correspondence only, unverified
note: The source ayah labels al-insan with root ء ن س; Daniel's Aramaic vision uses anash for a human-like figure coming with the clouds, a distinct singular use of the table's tentative correspondence rather than the commentary's general humanity.

basis: human-like figure receives dominion and an everlasting kingdom
note: Daniel gives the human-like figure dominion and a kingdom serving all peoples; this adds an exalted apocalyptic human counter-image to the commentary's human set as target and the ayah's general loss.

basis: truth cast to the ground
note: The commentary cites God hurling truth against falsehood; Daniel's hostile horn casts truth to the ground while acting successfully, reversing the agent, direction and immediate outcome of the cast.

basis: خ س ر / חסר; table sound correspondence
note: The commentary's loss follows a wrong course; a covenant curse says Israel will serve enemies in hunger, thirst and lack of everything, making Hebrew deficiency an outcome of disobedience in its context.

basis: word near in mouth and heart in order to do it
note: Deuteronomy places the command in mouth and heart so it can be done; this joins inward reception to action, sharpening the commentary's image of haqq entering the body and amal as force put to work.

basis: obedience without turning
note: The commentary's right action proceeds without deviating; Moses orders Israel to act as commanded and not turn right or left, a law shaped version of the unswerving course.

basis: Arabic source root خ س ر / Hebrew חסר; table's sound correspondence only, unverified
note: The commentary glosses source khusr as loss and deviation; Qoheleth says the crooked cannot be straightened and what is lacking cannot be counted, giving the tentative root pairing a concrete lack sense alongside the commentary's missed line.

basis: crooked cannot be straightened; lack cannot be counted
note: Qoheleth pairs an unstraightenable crooked thing with an uncountable lack; this directly joins the commentary's khusr-as-deviation to loss, but leaves the image as an irreparable defect rather than a missed thrust.

basis: crooked and lacking together
note: The commentary makes loss a deviation from the line; Qoheleth places what cannot be straightened beside what is lacking and cannot be counted, joining crookedness and deficiency without equating them.

basis: Arabic source root ع م ل / Hebrew עמל; table's sound correspondence only, unverified
note: The commentary labels the source word وَعَمِلُوا root ع م ل and describes acting with the spear; Qoheleth's Hebrew עמל is toil, and the question of what profit human labor yields adds the possibility of effort without gain while keeping the root link tentative.

basis: ع م ل / עמל; table sound correspondence
note: The commentary reads Arabic amal as effort put to work; Ecclesiastes asks what profit a human has from all his Hebrew amal under the sun, testing whether strenuous effort yields gain.

basis: blunt iron takes more force; wisdom brings success
note: Qoheleth says blunt iron requires more strength, while wisdom helps one succeed; this is a concrete tool-and-force image beside the commentary's spear, whose directed action must make an effective strike.

basis: ع م ل / עמל; table sound correspondence
note: The commentary's worked force is aimed at a result; Qoheleth reviews his handiwork and toil, calls it vapor and finds no gain, giving the same root's Hebrew toil a counterpoint of frustrated outcome.

basis: one companion lifts the other when he falls
note: The passage says one companion can lift the other after a fall; this makes the commentary's mutual counsel to patience practical support against a person's loss of footing.

basis: Arabic source roots ع م ل / Hebrew עמל and خ س ر / Hebrew חסר; both table correspondences unverified
note: Qoheleth describes unending toil and asks why the solitary worker labors while depriving himself of good; the verse brings the table's tentative work and lack correspondences together as effort that leaves a person without its benefit, contrasting the commentary's aimed action.

basis: two workers have good return for their toil
note: Qoheleth says two are better than one because their toil has a good return; this gives the commentary's action and mutual counsel a concrete cooperative setting, in which shared effort improves the result.

basis: ع م ل / עמל; table sound correspondence
note: The commentary couples effective work to mutual counsel; Qoheleth says two are better than one because they have a good reward for their Hebrew toil, supplying a concrete benefit to shared effort.

basis: خ س ر / חסר; table sound correspondence
note: The commentary calls loss a moral deviation; Qoheleth describes a wealthy person lacking nothing desired yet unable to enjoy it, showing that absence of Hebrew material lack can still coexist with frustrated gain.

basis: Aaron and Hur support Moses' arms until sunset
note: During Israel's battle with Amalek, companions physically hold Moses' tiring arms steady until sunset; this gives the commentary's counsel to sabr a communal image of sustaining effort rather than leaving endurance to an isolated person.

basis: prophets' words strike and kill
note: The commentary's haqq is a blow that reaches its object; God says he has hewn the people by prophets and killed them with the words of his mouth, linking speech to a bodily strike.

basis: ح ق ق / חקק; table sound correspondence
note: The commentary's haqq is the true course; Isaiah condemns rulers who enact unjust decrees, showing that a Hebrew ḥqq prescription can itself be crooked rather than true.

basis: unjust decree turns needy from justice
note: The commentary's haqq is a blow that does not deviate; the continuation of Isaiah's unjust decrees says they turn the needy aside from justice, spelling out the harmful deviation enacted by such rules.

basis: righteous judgment; rod of the mouth strikes earth; breath kills the wicked
note: Isaiah's just ruler judges the poor rightly, strikes the earth with his mouth's rod, and kills the wicked by his breath; this is a close verbal-impact counterpart to the commentary's haqq as a direct, penetrating blow against batil.

basis: mouth strikes and kills
note: The commentary reads haqq as a blow against what deviates; the ideal ruler strikes the earth with the rod of his mouth and kills the wicked with the breath of his lips, making just speech effective force.

basis: justice as line; righteousness as plumb; lies swept away
note: Isaiah makes justice the measuring line and righteousness the plumb, then says hail sweeps away refuge in lies; the commentary's loss-as-deviation and haqq-as-force meet in a judgment that aligns and destroys false shelter.

basis: voice directs the way
note: The commentary's mutual counsel of truth keeps action on course; a guiding voice says this is the way to walk when the hearers would turn right or left.

basis: crooked ground made straight for the Lord's road
note: Isaiah's return-road vision levels rough ground and makes crooked places straight; this gives the commentary's khusr-as-deviation a literal road image and a restoration context.

basis: mouth like sharp sword; servant as polished arrow
note: Isaiah describes the servant's mouth as a sharp sword and the servant as an arrow hidden in God's quiver; this joins speech to a force that can reach its target, as the commentary does with haqq and the penetrating lance.

basis: mouth sword and polished arrow
note: The commentary treats truth as a directed penetrating force; the servant says God made his mouth a sharp sword and made him a polished arrow, joining speech to a prepared projectile.

basis: all turn to their own way
note: The commentary says the human is in loss understood as deviation; the servant poem says all have wandered like sheep and each has turned to his own way, then places their iniquity on the servant.

basis: sent word accomplishes its purpose and does not return empty
note: Isaiah compares God's sent word to rain that makes the earth fruitful and says it accomplishes its purpose; this is a precise counter-image to the commentary's missed strike, where the true word reaches its intended result.

basis: word reaches its assigned result
note: The commentary's worked blow does not swerve or miss; God's outgoing word will not return empty but will accomplish the purpose for which he sent it, making successful arrival central without a weapon image.

basis: truth stumbles in public
note: The commentary gives truth an effective strike against falsehood; Isaiah instead portrays truth stumbling in the public square while justice is turned back, a specific reversal of truth's immediate success.

basis: truth absent and upright person prey
note: The commentary says the faithful escape loss by truth and right conduct; Isaiah says truth is missing and the one who turns from evil becomes prey, exposing a contrary outcome for the upright.

basis: God's word as fire and a hammer breaking rock
note: Jeremiah compares God's word to fire and a hammer that shatters rock; this gives the commentary's haqq-as-projectile a second image of forceful impact and adds the destruction of hard resistance.

basis: word as shattering hammer
note: The commentary says truth thrown upon falsehood breaks its target; God compares his word to fire and to a hammer that breaks rock, making authoritative speech a destroying force.

basis: Torah written within and on the heart
note: In the new-covenant promise, God writes Torah on the people's inward parts and hearts; this gives the commentary's penetrating strike an inward inscription counterpart and makes its truth a lasting disposition.

basis: prophetic words made fire that consumes the people
note: God makes his words in Jeremiah's mouth fire and the people wood to be consumed; this turns speech into a forceful strike, while casting its target as a resistant people under judgment.

basis: words made fire in mouth
note: The commentary's truth becomes an effective weapon; God tells Jeremiah he will make the words in the prophet's mouth fire and this people wood for it to consume.

basis: lost sheep wander from course
note: The commentary defines loss as straying; God calls his people lost sheep whom shepherds led astray on mountains, giving loss an agent and a wandering route.

basis: deceitful tongue as arrow
note: The commentary's penetrating projectile carries haqq; Jeremiah calls the deceitful tongue a deadly arrow even as the speaker offers a neighbor peace, assigning the weapon to false speech.

basis: speaker set up as God's target
note: Job says God seized and shattered him, then set him up as a target; it concretizes the commentary's human-as-target image as unwanted divine assault rather than a righteous blow.

basis: human set as target
note: The commentary's secondary sense of sabr makes a human the fixed target; Job says God set him up as a target after breaking him, shifting the blow onto a suffering person.

basis: archers pierce the kidneys
note: Job's complaint continues with archers surrounding him and an arrow piercing his kidneys; this matches the commentary's lance reaching the body's inside, but casts the hit as merciless suffering.

basis: arrows penetrate inward
note: The commentary's thrust reaches the belly; Job says archers surround him and God pierces his kidneys, a contrary scene in which the inward wound belongs to the human target.

basis: ح ق ق / חקק; table sound correspondence
note: The commentary gives the successful blow a fixed line; God says he prescribed the sea's bounds and set its bars and doors, a Hebrew enactment of a limit that controls movement.

basis: ء ن س / אנש; table sound correspondence, BDB note
note: The commentary's insan is exposed to loss except under right conduct; Eliphaz asks whether Hebrew enosh, mortal man, can be just before God, making human frailty a question about righteousness.

basis: man made a target
note: The commentary associates the human being with a target set up for a strike; Job asks God why he has made Job his target, giving that secondary image a direct human voice.

basis: person as target for bow
note: The commentary's human target and directed weapon meet the speaker's claim that God bent his bow and made him the target of an arrow; here the person receives the attack.

basis: weapon enters body
note: The commentary's blow penetrates to the interior; the lament says arrows from God's quiver entered the speaker's kidneys, developing the bodily result of being made a target.

basis: Arabic source root ح ق ق / Hebrew חקק; table's sound correspondence, unverified
note: The source commentary uses haqq for the direct, right blow; Nehemiah calls God's judgments straight, Torah true, and statutes good, giving the table's tentative ح ق ق / חקק correspondence a normative law-and-truth setting without claiming the roots are proven cognates.

basis: خ س ر / חסר; table sound correspondence
note: The commentary's exception from loss requires sustained right direction; Nehemiah recalls God sustaining Israel for forty wilderness years so they lacked nothing, giving Hebrew lack a historical case of provision on a journey.

basis: instruction is path, rejection misleads
note: The commentary's exhortation prevents departure from the true line; Proverbs puts heeding instruction on a path to life and says rejecting reproof leads astray.

basis: خ س ر / חסר; table sound correspondence
note: The commentary's loss is linked to error; Proverbs contrasts righteous lips that feed many with fools dying for lack of sense, a concrete moral and verbal setting for Hebrew deficiency.

basis: integrity guides, crookedness destroys
